lessons.title: Upstream switches ctor from module-global to self.* class-attr → swap-hack breaks; version-guard + set class attr
lessons.symptom: vllm-ascend subclasses an upstream model ctor via a module-global swap hack (e.g. swapping `qwen3_dflash.DFlashQwen3Model`/`DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer` globals around `super().__init__()`). Upstream later adds `decoder_layer_cls`/`model_cls` class attributes and changes the base ctor to `self.decoder_layer_cls(...)` / `self.model_cls(...)`. The swap-hack silently stops working because class-attribute lookups ignore module globals — DFlash2 draft builds the base DFlash1 model (no candidate_selector → AttributeError later).
lessons.root_cause: The base ctor resolves the overridable class through `self.<attr>` (class attribute) instead of a module-global reference. The ascend monkeypatch swapped the module global, which the new lookup no longer consults. On the old release (v0.27.1) the module-global reference still exists, so the swap is still needed there.
fix_guidance: Grep the upstream base ctor to confirm whether it uses `self.<class_attr>` or a module-global reference.
If it uses `self.<class_attr>` on main: add the matching class attribute to the ascend subclass (e.g. `model_cls = DFlash2Qwen3Model`, `decoder_layer_cls = DFlash2Qwen3DecoderLayer`).

Keep the module-global swap but guard it: `if vllm_version_is("0.27.1"): <swap hack> else: super().__init__(...)`. The class attributes are harmless on the old release because the old base ctor never reads them.
Verify the swap-hack is removed from the main lane so no dead global mutation remains, and both branches pass identical args to super().__init__().
